title: Inflight cache mismatch sleuthing
summary: Scratchpad for investigating an incident where in-flight requests hit inconsistent KV/prefix caches across regions and triggered fallback routing that increased tail latency.
content:
Goal:
- Capture commands/notes while I chase a hypothesis: regional cache key derivation mismatch + concurrent handoff caused smart-router to mark nodes unhealthy and trigger fallbacks to a slower model variant.

Observed symptoms (from metrics + quick grep):
- Spike in tail latency (p99 -> 2.8s) for a subset of requests between 2026-03-09T17:20Z and ~17:35Z.
- Concurrent increase in fallback_rate for route /v1/generate-chat in eu-west-1 -> routed to fallback pool (smaller n1 instances + non-quantized model).
- Error logs show repeated KV cache misses with identical request ids (see snippets below).

Useful log snippets (redacted):
- serving-runtime (eu-west-1):
  [2026-03-09T17:21:08Z] WARN kv_cache: miss key=prefix:a1b2c3 session=svc-743 user=acct-999
  [2026-03-09T17:21:09Z] ERROR router: connection reset by peer while streaming response to client_id=cli-1123 route=/v1/generate-chat
  [2026-03-09T17:21:09Z] WARN router: marking backend pool "model-nominal-eu-1" unhealthy (5 failures in 10s)

- api-gateway: 429 / 503 spike around same time, requests rerouted to dedicated fallback pools.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Cache key derivation misalignment between regions: a serialization/locale difference (e.g., floating truncation or header ordering) produced different cache keys so prefetched KV entries were not hit when requests crossed AZ/regional boundaries.
2) Short TTL / stale cache eviction + sudden traffic shift caused many concurrent cold misses which overloaded model nodes (warmup cost), router interpreted delay as failures and ejected pool -> fallback.
3) Race in handoff logic: when routing decision moves an open session from pool A->B during autoscaling, in-flight KV references point to pool-local cache causing repeated misses.
4) Network flakiness caused a burst of connection resets and router fallback policy kicked in; cache misses are consequential, not causal.

Commands I ran / should run (timestamps approximate):
- Prometheus queries (grafana -> explore):
  - increase(rate(router_fallback_total[1m])) by region
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(model_response_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le,region,model))

- From control host (eu-west-1 box):
  # tail logs while reproducing
  ssh infra-eu1
  sudo journalctl -u serving-runtime -f | grep --line-buffered "kv_cache\|router\|fallback"

- Inspect cache keys in memcached/redis (read-only):
  redis-cli -h redis-eu-01 HGETALL "prefix:a1b2c3"  # returned nothing during spike
  redis-cli -h redis-us-02 HGETALL "prefix:a1b2c3"  # returned entry (shows mismatch)

- Reproduce locally (dev model) using curl sequence to emulate prefix caching:
  for i in {1..50}; do \
    curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" -d '{"prompt":"test prefix $i"}' \
    | jq '.meta.kv_key' >> /tmp/keys_eu.txt; done

  for i in {1..50}; do \
    curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "X-Region: us-west-2" -d '{"prompt":"test prefix $i"}' \
    | jq '.meta.kv_key' >> /tmp/keys_us.txt; done

  diff /tmp/keys_eu.txt /tmp/keys_us.txt  # look for derivation differences

- Grep for suspicious serializer changes in recent commits:
  git log --stat --since="2 weeks ago" -- path/to/prefix_key_serializer.py

Notes on telem / metrics names to check: router_fallback_total, kv_cache_miss_total, kv_cache_hit_ratio, model_warmup_duration_seconds, pool_ejects_total, connection_reset_total, route_rps_by_region.

What I tried and results:
- Ran diff of generated keys from eu vs us (dev): found ordering difference when prompt contains embedded JSON with unordered maps -> serializer produced different string across python's json.dumps call with sort_keys=False.
  -> Reproduced: when request body has metadata map, keys emitted in different orders depending on python version/environment.
- Temporarily forced json.dumps(sort_keys=True) in local dev: key derivation aligned across regions and local replay showed much higher cache hit ratio.
- Applied a hotfix on a single eu staging instance (set sort_keys=True) and ran synthetic traffic: kv_cache_miss_total dropped from ~45% -> 6% for the synthetic workload, p99 improved from 1.8s -> 0.35s.
- However, production rollout of same change is non-trivial because serializer is in shared lib used by other teams and we need broader testing.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How many production pools were affected? Need to correlate pool_ejects_total by pool name + time window.
- Did the router mark pools unhealthy because of increased latency (backpressure) or real connection errors? Check connection_reset_total and underlying TCP logs.
- Was any autoscaler action (scale down/up) coincident with the event? If so, that could exacerbate handoffs.
- Are there clients sending inconsistent headers (Accept-Language, timezone) that feed into key derivation?

Quick checklist for next runs (minimal blast radius):
- Reproduce in staging with mixed-region traffic: generate identical request shapes from eu and us clients and assert identical kv_key.
- Add temporary server-side assert to log both computed key and canonicalized payload hash when in debug mode.
- Query logs for commits touching common serializer libs in last 30 days.
- Run a rolling canary (5% traffic) with sort_keys=True and telemetry baked in (track kv_cache_hit_ratio, fallback_rate).
- Have fallback policy temporarily relax pool-ejection sensitivity for 10m during canary (to avoid mass fallback while caches rebuild).

Incident timeline (rough):
- 17:18Z: slight increase in kv cache miss ratio in eu-west-1 (observed in metrics)
- 17:20Z: first router pool ejects recorded for model-nominal-eu-1
- 17:21–17:26Z: fallback rate spike, p99 latency spike
- 17:27Z: small rollback of a recent client-facing serializer change (not confirmed)
- 17:30Z: manual mitigation: raise ejection threshold, spin up extra warm nodes in eu-west-1
- 17:40Z: traffic normalized; full recovery by 17:55Z

Manual checks performed after recovery:
- grep for serializer changes in deploys that hit eu nodes: found PR #981 touched prefix key serialization.
- cross-region key sampling confirmed mismatch for complex prompts only (large nested JSON).

Follow-ups / actions to propose (for RFC):
- Require deterministic serialization for any field that participates in cache key derivation (document the invariant).
- Add a canonicalization library in serving-runtime with unit tests across python versions and languages (JS/Go) used by gateways.
- Improve router ejection heuristics to take into account cache_miss_rate spikes vs connection errors (differentiate failure modes).
- Add a short-term feature: when many concurrent misses observed, throttle eviction and prefer warm-up/backoff instead of immediate pool ejection.

Notes-to-self: keep this scratch doc alive while I gather exact counts; will move to shared postmortem if hypothesis confirmed. Tagging Aisha to help correlate pool metrics and Keisha for rollout plan.

Unresolved commands to run next:
- bigquery: SELECT count(*) FROM telemetry.request_keys WHERE kv_key IS NULL AND region='eu-west-1' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-09 17:15:00' AND '2026-03-09 17:40:00';
- prom: increase(sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (pool,region))
- infra: capture tcpdump on a sample backend during replay to detect connection resets (if still reproducible).

Scratch ends.

-- Diego M.
